TICK SCOPE (deterministic — computed by diffing the board fingerprint since the last consumed tick):
board issues: CHANGED 561 "a" (comments: 1 -> 2)
board issues: CHANGED 562 "b" (comments: 3 -> 4)

Work ONLY the tickets listed above this tick: fetch each one's full comment thread and act on it per the SOP below. An UNBLOCKED line names a child that is launchable on the DEFAULT BRANCH now — either its Blocked-by ticket is CLOSED with no other blocker open, or the line says 'dep-verified soft', which means the harness checked those still-open blockers against this child's planned files and its own plan and found no code dependency (bin/dep-verify.sh), or it says 'dep-unverified, released', which means the check had no evidence yet and DEP_UNKNOWN_MODE=soft releases the child anyway (the merge conductor rebases it if a real overlap surfaces). Any of those ways, fetch it and launch it per the queue rules unless a PR or a build already covers it. A STACKABLE line is JUST AS LAUNCHABLE: its Blocked-by ticket is still open, but that parent's PR is open, so the child builds ON TOP of the parent's branch — launch it exactly like an UNBLOCKED one and pass the base branch through, `STACK_BASE=<the line's base= value> setsid /root/harness/bin/run-build.sh ...` (everything else about the launch is unchanged; GitHub retargets the child's PR to the default branch when the parent merges). SKIP the full board/ticket enumeration the SOP opens with — unchanged tickets have not moved since the last consumed run and owe nothing new. You MAY fetch any other specific ticket that a changed thread references or depends on. Queue and build-results handling in the SOP still applies as written. If the scope list looks inconsistent with what you actually fetch (a listed ticket is missing, ids look stale), discard the scope and run the full SOP instead.

SOP for project-5. Fetch the thread. Do the work.

FILE-OVERLAP GUARD (deterministic — run it, do not reason about it). Immediately before you launch a build for a ticket, run `/root/harness/bin/overlap-guard.sh project-5 <KEY>`. It answers LAUNCH (go — every error answers LAUNCH too, except an unreadable open-PR list with no cached copy, which DEFERs as `DEFER <KEY> gh unknown …`) or DEFER, and a DEFER names the sibling build or open PR whose files collide. On DEFER do NOT launch that ticket this tick: leave its queue line in place, and say in your output which key deferred and on which files. The next tick re-offers it — this is BUILD_DEFERRED semantics, not a queue and not a wait.
